solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Did suit check, even by itself?

definitions.meaning: ... with means agreed with or suited, as in a story that ... with the facts
... paper is checked, marked out in a grid of small squares
a debt that is ... is settled, leaving both sides even
a number ... is multiplied by itself

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about a card player who followed suit and checked, apparently on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: Four definitions run together. 'Did suit' reads as a card-playing action but is the past tense of square with, meaning matched.
explanation.definitionFit: Each piece is a separate sense of the word: agreed, chequered, settled and multiplied by itself.

clue.text: Priority for egoist suffering from dual personality that goes viral

indicators.note: someone with a split personality is two selves, so the egoist's word appears for each of them

parts.note: an egoist puts me first, so the word me is the egoist's top priority

explanation.surface: A self-obsessed person with a split personality whose content spreads online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering from dual personality' doubles ME: each personality insists on itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A meme is an image, phrase or video copied and shared rapidly online, the thing that goes viral.

clue.text: Act unrestrainedly on cycle three times

indicators.note: cycling the phrase round means its opening letters are taken from the front and put back at the end

parts.note: to let rip is to act without any restraint

explanation.surface: Someone goes wild on a bike ride, three times over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on cycle' moves LE from the front of LETRIP to the back, giving TRIP + LE. 'Act unrestrainedly' wants to be the definition; it is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Triple as an adverb-like multiplier means threefold, or three times as much.

clue.text: Games giant's no plan to enter

indicators.note: the plan is to enter the word no, so it is placed inside it

parts.note: to plan to do something is to intend it

explanation.surface: A big video-game company announces it has no plans to enter a market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' is taken literally as letters, not as a refusal; the plan goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nintendo is the Japanese company behind Mario and the Switch, one of the biggest names in video gaming.

clue.text: 'Please do not power up' — checking date, it's an old, old flyer

indicators.note: the reversed letters hold the date in check, so it sits within them
in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: no, don't is a plea not to do something, as a hesitant date might say
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
an era is a date in the sense of a period of time

explanation.surface: A warning notice not to switch on, checking a date, about an ancient aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NO DON'T + P into PTNODON, and 'checking' puts ERA in after PT.
explanation.definitionFit: The pteranodon was a flying reptile of the Cretaceous, so very old indeed, which the doubled old stresses.

clue.text: Remove perfume from line?

parts.note: the prefix de- means remove, as in de-ice or defrost
a scent is a perfume

explanation.surface: An instruction to get rid of the fragrance from a washing line.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as DE-SCENT, literally to remove a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Descent means ancestry or lineage, so a family line is one's descent.

clue.text: First to examine question of concern about King or Queen?

definitions.text: First to examine question of concern about King or Queen?

indicators.note: the first of the word examine supplies only its opening letter
the question goes around the royal letter, which sits inside it

parts.note: a query is a question raised out of concern
R stands for Rex (king) or Regina (queen)

explanation.surface: Who is first to look into anything troubling the monarch?
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside QUERY after E. R works for both Rex and Regina, hence 'King or Queen'.
explanation.definitionFit: An equerry is an officer of the royal household who attends the sovereign, the first to look into royal concerns.

clue.text: RU team's wages finally withdrawn, papers being collected

indicators.note: the papers are collected up inside the other letters

parts.note: a fee is payment for work, a wage
I (the i newspaper) and FT (Financial Times) are both British papers

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of withdrawn

explanation.surface: A rugby team's pay is stopped, with the newspapers gathering the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being collected' puts I and FT after the F of FEE + N.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rugby Union side has fifteen players, so the team is called a fifteen.

clue.text: Scene of iconic kiss (x) — make that 'xx'?

definitions.meaning: the New York square where a sailor famously kissed a nurse on V-J Day
x is the multiplication sign, read as times; xx is times multiplied by itself

explanation.surface: A puzzled correction about how many kisses to sign off with, since x is a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: The x looks like a kiss at the end of a message, but read it as the sign for times; doubling it to xx squares it.
explanation.definitionFit: Times Square in New York is where the famous V-J Day photo of a sailor kissing a nurse was taken.

clue.text: Prove what N, E, or S would normally do in 16 — but not W, oddly

definitions.meaning: to establish an argument, to prove something

definitions.text: what N, E, or S would normally do in 16 — but not W, oddly
definitions.meaning: in Scrabble the tiles N, E and S each score one point, while W scores four

explanation.surface: Compass points in a game, where north, east and south behave but west does not.
explanation.walkthrough: N, E, S and W look like compass points; they are Scrabble tiles, and 16 is SCRABBLE. 'oddly' means unusually, not odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a point is to argue successfully for something, so to prove it; literally, a one-point tile makes a point.

clue.text: What's needed for 16 19s — a stretcher!

definitions.meaning: 16 is SCRABBLE and 19 is LETTER, so this is the stand that holds a player's Scrabble tiles
a torture device that stretched its victim

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the game's pieces need something to lie on, like a medical stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretcher' suggests the hospital kind; here it is the torture rack that stretches people.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scrabble player keeps tiles on a rack, and the medieval rack was a device for stretching prisoners.

clue.text: Good judge of taste? This chap's broken new tea set!

indicators.note: this chap has broken into the set, so he sits inside the other letters
a new arrangement of the letters of tea set is needed

parts.note: he is the pronoun for this chap

explanation.surface: A man of refined taste is blamed for smashing a brand-new tea set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges TEA SET and 'broken' makes this chap break into it, splitting the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is someone with a cultivated appreciation of beauty and art, a connoisseur of taste.

clue.text: In confidence university stores don't supply powder

indicators.note: the confidence word with its university letter stores the rearranged letters inside it

parts.note: U, the abbreviation for university, placed in TRUST, a word for confidence

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A university, told something in confidence, refuses to hand over the powder it keeps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb but is the adverb of supple, meaning flexibly, so it signals a rearrangement. 'In' puts U into TRUST, and 'stores' keeps the rearranged letters after its R.
explanation.definitionFit: To powder, as a verb, is to crumble into fine particles, which is what turning to dust means.

clue.text: Girl's group debut song — a hit, not a failure

definitions.text: Girl's group debut song — a hit

parts.note: no means not a, as in no fool
a no-no is something that fails, a thing that just won't do

explanation.surface: A girl band's first single was a success rather than a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is three of the same word, Elgar's own example of a triple word.
explanation.definitionFit: No, No, No was Destiny's Child's debut single, a hit for the girl group in 1997.

clue.text: In our bag you'll find small spar

indicators.note: the small letter goes in the word for our bag

parts.note: a person's bag is their thing; for setters and solvers that is crosswords
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone finds a little piece of rigging or mineral in their shopping bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our bag' is slang for our special interest, crosswords; S goes after CROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to argue or fight, and to cross swords is the idiom for coming into conflict.

clue.text: The dimensions of its playing surface 8 and 1 put together from scratch

definitions.text: The dimensions of its playing surface 8 and 1 put together
definitions.meaning: 8 is FIFTEEN and 1 is SQUARED, and the board game's board is fifteen squared, fifteen by fifteen
to scratch or scrape about with the hands

explanation.surface: A game whose board is fifteen by fifteen, built up from nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 and 1 refer to FIFTEEN and SQUARED in this grid. 'from' is a link: the answer comes from the sense scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble is the word game on a 15 by 15 board, and to scrabble is to scratch or claw at something.

clue.text: Sorry eggs John regularly takes Lord

indicators.note: the selected letters of John take the other letters inside them
regularly takes alternate letters of John, the first and third

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying sorry? when you did not hear
ova is the plural of ovum, an egg

explanation.surface: John apologises for eggs and takes the Lord's name, a breakfast confession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the odd letters of John, J and H, and 'takes' means they hold the rest between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Jehovah is a form of the Hebrew name of God, who is addressed as Lord.

clue.text: Law #1: study vocabulary

parts.note: lex is Latin for law
number one, written as the Roman numeral I
to con is an old word for to study or learn

explanation.surface: A rule of thumb for students: the first law is to learn your words.
explanation.walkthrough: To con, meaning to study, survives mostly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon is the stock of words of a language or person, so a vocabulary.

clue.text: I say, landord's one who must make allowances

definitions.meaning: the ... I, for example, so I is a ...
a landlord lets property, so is one who lets
one who lets, permits or allows

explanation.surface: A tenant remarks that the landlord is the one who has to be tolerant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' sounds like an exclamation; read it as I, say, an example of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter is an alphabet symbol, someone who rents out property, and anyone who allows something.

clue.text: Not impressed by turns, A.N. Other opened shows on tour

indicators.note: a show on tour goes round, so this word goes around the other letters

parts.note: undid means opened, as with a parcel or a button

indicators.note: taking letters by turns means every other letter of A.N. Other

explanation.surface: An unnamed person, unimpressed by a run of shows they opened on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: A.N. Other is the stock placeholder name; 'by turns' takes its even letters N, T, E. 'shows on tour' means going round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Undinted means bearing no dent, so not impressed in the physical sense of not having been pressed in.

clue.text: Within reach, but ultimately you'll have to oust a big shot

indicators.note: the final letter will have to push out the letter a and take its place

parts.note: something within reach is doable

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of you, the word before the contraction

parts.note: you'll is you will, so the word you is the one being cut

explanation.surface: A tip that a shot within range will still need you to knock out a top gunman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately you' gives U, which 'have to oust' swaps for the A in DOABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is a twice-normal measure of spirits, so a large shot at the bar.

clue.text: Promise a choice between seven days and one?

indicators.note: the conjunction offering a choice sits between the two time letters

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for week, seven days
one here is one day, abbreviated D
or is the conjunction that offers a choice between options

explanation.surface: Someone asked to pledge chooses between a week and a single day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' means one of the days, D, matching W for 'seven days'.
explanation.definitionFit: To give your word is to promise, so a word means a pledge or assurance.

clue.text: Tackle Drambuie shot, inhaling essence of herbs — grand!

indicators.note: the rearranged liqueur breathes in the herb letter, taking it inside
shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are reworked
the essence is the central letter of herbs

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A shot of the herbal whisky liqueur Drambuie, sniffed and found grand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges DRAMBUIE to BERMUDAI and 'inhaling' takes R inside after BERMUDA. Tackle in sailing is rigging, not a lunge.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bermuda rig is the triangular-sail arrangement on most modern yachts, a type of sailing tackle.

clue.text: A crossword great, I — wonderstruck — am blown away!

indicators.note: am is blown away, so those letters are removed from the word

parts.note: amazed means struck with wonder

explanation.surface: A solver gasps in admiration at a legendary setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am blown away' removes AM from the front of AMAZED.
explanation.definitionFit: Azed is the long-running pseudonym of the Observer's barred-grid setter, a giant of crosswords.

clue.text: I forgot to mention a clue teasingly written about seed-case

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are written around the postscript, which sits inside
a clue written teasingly is twisted, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: PS, a postscript, adds what the writer forgot to mention

explanation.surface: A setter adds a postscript that a clue was cheekily written about a seed pod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teasingly' rearranges A CLUE to CAULE; 'written about' wraps it round the postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a capsule is a dry fruit that splits open to release seeds, a seed-case.

clue.text: Stuck here? Puzzled, I'll give up and let go

indicators.note: puzzled suggests confusion, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A baffled solver, stuck, decides to give up and let go of the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuck here?' is a cryptic hint: things are stuck in a gluepot.
explanation.definitionFit: A gluepot holds glue, so anything inside would be stuck there; it also means a sticky situation.
